name: gbti-terminal-sessions
description: Save terminal sessions as reusable profiles (shell, directory and startup commands) and bring them back after a restart. Also repositions the Explorer, terminal and chat panes as collapsible columns.

commands.title: Move Global Profiles into This Workspace

viewsWelcome.contents:
No saved instance profiles yet.

A profile is a saved terminal setup: which shell to open, where, and what to run once it is ready.

[New Profile](command:terminalSessions.profiles.new)

You can also right-click a terminal tab and choose "Save as Instance Profile" to start from one you already have open.

terminalSessions.columns.markdownDescription: Columns to control, in status-bar order. Leave empty to use the built-in defaults (Files, Editor, Terminal, Chat).

id.description: Stable identifier used to persist visibility.

label.description: Text shown on the status-bar chip.

kind.markdownDescription:
Which workbench container this column controls.

`editor` is not independent of the others: VS Code hides the editor area by **maximizing the panel** over it, so the editor's space goes to the `panel` column and the two can never be hidden together. Hiding the editor reveals the panel if it was closed.

Whichever columns you list, one always stays visible: the last one refuses to hide.

viewId.markdownDescription: Command run when revealing, choosing which view appears, for example `workbench.view.explorer` or `workbench.view.scm`.

position.description: For 'panel' columns: which edge the panel occupies.

terminalSessions.layout.autoEnable.markdownDescription:
Bring the column layout back on startup if it was enabled when the window closed. Affects the columns only. Session profiles and restore are independent and have no on/off switch.

A layout you turned off with **Disable Column Layout** stays off regardless.

terminalSessions.autoEnable.markdownDeprecationMessage: Renamed to `#terminalSessions.layout.autoEnable#`, since it only ever governed the column layout. Still read if the new setting is unset.
terminalSessions.autoEnable.description: Restore the layout automatically on startup if it was enabled when the window closed.

enumDescriptions: Save new profiles in this project's .vscode/settings.json, so they appear only here.
Save new profiles in your user settings, so they appear in every project.
terminalSessions.profileScope.markdownDescription:
The scope a **new** profile starts at.

Each profile carries its own scope, set from the **Saved in** control in the profile editor; this only seeds the initial value. The sidebar always lists this project's profiles plus any global ones, marking the global ones.

Falls back to global in a window with no folder open, where workspace settings cannot be written.

terminalSessions.instanceProfiles.markdownDescription: Saved terminal setups. Set here in your user settings they appear in every project; set in a project's `.vscode/settings.json` they appear only there, and a workspace profile shadows a global one of the same name. Authored via `Save as Instance Profile` on a terminal's right-click menu, and hand-editable here. Commands are replayed **literally**: write `claude --resume Alpha` to reopen that exact session each time, or `claude --continue` to rejoin whatever ran last in `cwd`.

name.description: Profile name, also used as the terminal tab name.

distro.description: WSL distro to enter. Implies wsl.exe -d <distro> as the shell.

shellPath.description: Explicit shell for non-WSL profiles. Ignored when 'distro' is set.

cwd.description: Working directory. A Linux path when 'distro' is set, otherwise a host path.

commands.markdownDescription:
Commands run in order once the shell is ready. Every command but the last is awaited, so a long-running process such as `claude` belongs last.

Either a plain string, or `{ "run": "...", "waitMs": 5000 }` to override how long to allow before that command runs. On the first command that is how long shell integration is given to activate; on later ones it caps how long the previous may take. Default 3000.

waitMs.description: Milliseconds to allow before this command runs.

showInDropdown.description: Mirror this profile into VS Code's terminal + dropdown.

terminalSessions.autoRestoreSession.markdownDescription: Reopen saved profiles automatically on startup. Safe by construction: only commands you wrote into a profile yourself are ever run, and a terminal whose process genuinely survived is left alone rather than replaced.

terminalSessions.restoreDelayMs.description: How long to wait after startup before restoring, so VS Code's own terminal revival finishes first and tabs are not duplicated.

terminalSessions.layout.autoEnableEveryw.markdownDescription:
Bring the column layout up in every workspace, including ones where it has never been enabled. Set to `false` to opt in per project by clicking a chip.

Affects the columns only. **Disable Column Layout** still wins in the workspace where you ran it, so an explicit choice is not overridden by this.

terminalSessions.autoEnableEverywhere.markdownDeprecationMessage: Renamed to `#terminalSessions.layout.autoEnableEverywhere#`, since it only ever governed the column layout. Still read if the new setting is unset.
terminalSessions.autoEnableEverywhere.description: Enable automatically in every workspace, including ones where it has never been enabled. Set to false if you would rather opt in per project by clicking a chip.
